PullRequest.Title: Perf: Register built-in notebook types declaratively
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Register the Interactive Window notebook type declaratively instead of instantiating `INotebookService` during workbench restoration.

- Add a lightweight registry for built-in notebook type metadata.
- Register the Interactive notebook type at module load alongside its editor pane.
- Merge built-in types when `NotebookProviderInfoStore` is first materialized.
- Preserve built-in metadata over stale entries restored from the notebook-type memento.
- Keep Interactive editor resolver registration in `BlockRestore`.

## Startup scenario impact

The standard startup scenario restores one text editor and does not open an Interactive Window. Previously, `InteractiveDocumentContribution` still injected `INotebookService` and called `getContributedNotebookType('interactive')`.

That query materialized `NotebookProviderInfoStore`, which transitively initialized notebook, editor resolver, configuration, storage, file, and accessibility dependencies during blocking workbench restoration.

With this change, ordinary startup registers only lightweight editor resolver metadata. The Interactive notebook type remains globally declared, but its provider object and dependencies are materialized only when notebook provider information is actually needed.

## Measurements

Both variants were independently minified from the same source commit and overlaid onto the same Insiders runtime. The startup scenario restored one text editor in a deterministic folder with extensions and GPU acceleration disabled.

### Uninstrumented warm startup

30 per-start alternating pairs:

| Metric | Baseline | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median total startup | 1406 ms | 1398 ms |
| Median paired difference |  | **-7 ms** |
| Bootstrap 95% interval |  | **-14 ms to -1.5 ms** |

Critical phase markers:

| Marker | Paired difference | 95% interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Renderer startup | **-9 ms** | -12 ms to -3.5 ms |
| Workbench startup | **-5 ms** | -8 ms to -1 ms |
| Blocking contribution creation | **-2 ms** | -2 ms to -1 ms |

### Profiled renderer startup

Three measured warmed traces:

| Metric | Baseline | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `didStartRenderer` to `didStartWorkbench` | 1502.2 ms | 1475.5 ms (**-26.7 ms**) |
| `workbench.contrib.interactiveDocument` | 3.1-3.3 ms | **0.2-0.3 ms** |

Trace instrumentation increases absolute startup time, but all three traces show that the Interactive contribution no longer pulls the notebook provider initialization chain onto the startup critical path.

## Architecture and compatibility

- `InteractiveEditorInput` does not own global registration or reference-counting state.
- The built-in type registry follows VS Code's platform `Registry` pattern.
- Registrations return disposables, allowing tests and future non-process-lifetime consumers to clean up.
- The provider store owns the materialized provider entries and disposes them with its existing lifecycle.
- Interactive editor resolver registration remains blocking, so opening and restoring Interactive Windows continues to work.
- Existing cached notebook type metadata cannot conflict with the declarative built-in entry.

## Validation

- Full client compile and type-check
- Targeted ESLint
- Notebook provider registry unit tests
- Minified production bundle
- Interactive Window real-UI scenario:
  - Open an Interactive Window
  - Close it
  - Reopen it successfully
- Three paired startup traces
- 30 paired uninstrumented warm startup runs

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A blocking startup contribution forced a delayed notebook service and its provider store to instantiate solely to query/register the Interactive notebook type, eagerly executing synchronous constructor and metadata setup before any notebook use.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Ordinary workbench restoration paid notebook provider initialization work despite restoring no Interactive Window or notebook.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The Interactive notebook descriptor is now placed in a lightweight in-memory registry at module evaluation. NotebookProviderInfoStore consumes it only when notebook provider information is first requested, so ordinary startup no longer instantiates NotebookService/NotebookProviderInfoStore or performs their storage and extension-metadata setup on the BlockRestore critical path.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, the BlockRestore contribution constructor injected INotebookService at line 84 and immediately called getContributedNotebookType('interactive'); that method accesses NotebookService.notebookProviderInfoStore, whose lazy getter creates NotebookProviderInfoStore. The store constructor synchronously reads its storage memento, registers extension listeners/handler, and processes notebook/editor metadata. INotebookService is registered Delayed, so the constructor call defeated that laziness during blocking workbench restoration even when no notebook was opened. The diff removes both the injection and query and replaces them with one module-load metadata registration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ordinary workbench startup restoring a text editor with no notebook or Interactive Window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: InteractiveDocumentContribution still runs in BlockRestore to register two editor resolvers, but the changed module-level registration performs only one Map insertion. NotebookService and NotebookProviderInfoStore construction no longer have to complete before restoration progresses.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the notebook editor memento and install/process the notebooks extension-point handler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One store materialization, scanning the cached/contributed notebook types once; effective cardinality is the number of notebook type contributions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted INotebookService query forced the delayed service and provider store to materialize once during BlockRestore, placing this work on startup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: After the diff this boundary is not reached by ordinary Interactive contribution startup, so it no longer blocks BlockRestore.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One built-in Interactive descriptor at module load; the avoided deferred store work otherwise scales with cached and installed notebook type contributions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous and serial on the renderer startup path; there is no spawned concurrency or queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold and warm ordinary starts both register one in-memory built-in descriptor. The persisted notebook-type memento is not read by this contribution until provider information is actually requested; no negative cache or repeated miss is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted constructor dependency and query directly reached the lazy store getter, while the replacement is a single Map insertion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact startup milliseconds vary by machine and extension set, but the removed synchronous construction and its one-time metadata scan are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: This scenario is a concrete performance improvement and fixes eager startup work; it introduces no reportable regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: First opening or restoring an Interactive Window after startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: InteractiveEditorInput/model resolution requests INotebookService provider information. On a cold provider-store cache, NotebookProviderInfoStore must now materialize before the Interactive model can resolve; subsequent opens use the existing store.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the notebook type memento, process registered notebook extension contributions, and persist refreshed metadata through Memento when the extension-point handler runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per NotebookService lifetime, scanning each contributed notebook type once; the Interactive registry contributes exactly one additional descriptor and duplicate memento data is skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: BlockRestore had already materialized and populated the store before the user could open an Interactive Window, so first-open did not pay this portion itself.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold first use now pays this initialization; warm Interactive opens do not. This is the deliberate first-use side of removing the same work from every ordinary startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate/use the notebook serializer and resolve the Interactive notebook model when the editor opens.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical provider/model resolution per cold Interactive document, with existing service/model caches serving repeated use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same serializer activation and model resolution were required before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for first Interactive content; its operation count and scheduling are unchanged by the metadata registry change.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold initialization scales with installed notebook contributions, not cells or open editors; the changed built-in portion is constant cardinality one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous lazy initialization in the renderer; the later serializer/model operations retain their existing extension-host and model-service sequencing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold first use constructs the provider store once and merges the declarative descriptor ahead of stale memento entries. Warm use reuses the store. There is no repeated negative lookup or per-open registry scan.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the store getter is lazy and getContributedNotebookType reaches it, while module registration itself does not.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact cold-open latency depends on installed notebook contributions, but this is bounded one-time initialization and the PR intentionally trades that small cold-use cost for avoiding it on all non-notebook startups.
Scenarios.Verdict: The one-time work is intentionally deferred to actual notebook use and is neither duplicated nor amplified; no actionable performance finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: First generic notebook provider query and later extension contribution refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Any getContributedNotebookTypes/getContributedNotebookType call materializes the store, which consumes all currently registered built-in descriptors before cached and extension-provided entries. Extension-point setup then rebuilds provider metadata once.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load cached provider descriptors and register the existing extension-point handler, which serializes the resulting provider list to the storage memento.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One load/handler setup per store lifetime and one pass over effective unique provider IDs; the added duplicate guard prevents the built-in and stale cache entry from both being instantiated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same store and handler work occurred once during startup because the Interactive contribution forced the first query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs on the first provider query rather than during Interactive BlockRestore; subsequent provider queries are in-memory Map lookups.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of built-in descriptors plus unique persisted/extension notebook provider IDs. This PR adds one built-in entry and skips its stale duplicate.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous serial map/array processing under the existing extension-point handler; no new parallel burst, per-item IPC, or subprocess work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Built-in metadata wins over a stale memento entry by ID, so effective cardinality remains one provider for 'interactive'. Store lifetime caching prevents repeated reconstruction; registration is process-lifetime and constant-size.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor loops and duplicate checks are explicit, and all accesses after construction use the retained Map.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future built-in registrations could increase the one-time linear scan, but the current diff registers only one and adds no unbounded source.
Scenarios.Verdict: No repeated boundary fan-out, unbounded retention, or cache lifecycle regression is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and all diff pages. The change replaces eager BlockRestore notebook-service/provider-store materialization with one constant-size declarative registry entry, preserves one-time store caching and unique provider cardinality, and adds appropriate handler disposal. No diff-introduced performance finding met the reporting threshold; the verified eager-startup regression fix was recorded separately.
